topic.title: Projects and Publishing
topic.shortdesc: An introduction to projects in and how they support content management, review workflows, and publishing deliverables.

body.p: lets you manage DITA Projects. Users with the Author platform user role can create projects, import content, and manage its lifecycle from creation and review to publishing as PDF or Oxygen WebHelp Responsive.

section.title: What is a Project in Content Fusion?
section.p:
A Content Fusion Project:
Provides Git-based storage for DITA content.
Allows authors to create content with AI assistance.
Provides a graphical interface to manage review tasks within the project.
Helps Authors build WebHelp or PDF outputs via Publications and Deliverables.

section.title: Main Projects Page
section.p: Projects is one of the two main components in the Content Fusion browser interface, along with Review Tasks. The main Projects page displays all projects that you can access.
To open an existing project, simply click on it. This opens the project's Publications page by default.

Click the star button to the far-right of the project card to specify it as a favorite. You can filter the list to only show the starred projects by selecting the Show only starred button at the top of the page.
You can also use the text filter field at the top to filter the list of projects by name or description.

section.title: Creating a New Project
section.p: Click the New project button to create a new project. This opens a dialog box where you can choose one of the following options:

ul.li:
Import from Git - Configure the connection to your Git repository. It includes the following fields:
Name - The name of the project.
Description - The description of the project. It is displayed under the project's name in the main Projects page.
Project URL - The URL of the Git repository.
Branch - The default branch for the project.
Visibility - You can choose between Public (accessible by all members) or Private (restricts access to select members).
Username and Access Token - Use this option to enter the Git credentials (username and access token).For details about how access tokens should be created and configured, see .
Git Account - Use this option to select a preconfigured Git account.
After you finish configuring the details, click Create project to complete the process.

Create from template - Choose from the following configuration options:
Choose template - Select one of the predefined templates to create a project. Available templates include:
An empty project.
A Software Docs Starter starter DITA XML project.
A project created from a template is stored internally in Content Fusion. Later, you can link an external Git repository, and all the content will be moved to that repository.
Name - The name of the project.
Description - The description of the project. It is displayed under the project's name in the main Projects page.
Visibility - You can choose between Public (accessible by all members) or Private (restricts access to select members).

Create sample project - You can choose from predefined templates to create a project:
Circle Chat - A sample software documentation project that showcases reuse and profiling.
Syncro Smartphone - A sample hardware documentation project that showcases the use of keyscopes and branch filtering.
Hydraulic Gear Pump - A sample hardware documentation project that showcases the use of an image map.
Sunny Sky - A sample API documentation project that showcases the inclusion of an OpenAPI JSON file in a DITA XML project.

section.p: The newly created project opens automatically with the project's Publications page displayed.

note.p: You can use a URL query parameter (in the form of /projects/new-from-url?url= to create a project from a Git repository. This is useful for advanced scenarios where you want to provide a project creation URL in documentation, tutorials, or as a button in a CMS.

The URL parameter accepts either a Git repository URL or a download archive URL generated by a Git server. For the archive URL option, the generated archive must contain a root folder where the content is located. You can also use the optional folder parameter to specify the folder that contains the content to use when creating the project.

body.note: When trying to merge branches inside the Personal Workspace, the merge cannot be processed if you have any local outgoing changes. In this case, a warning dialog box informs you that the outgoing changes must be committed or discarded before attempting the merge.
